bot_home_compact_lobby.title: Compact 10x15 | stone lobby and supplies
bot_home_compact_lobby.description: 10x15 stone lobby. Approved U translated into x=2..8/z=7..13: 29 barrels, 15 furnaces and crafting. Clear west passage and north approach; east fixture bank sits against the wall. Dry two-cell corner pit [6,0,2],[7,0,2], complete rim and two stair blocks; no extra foundation.

bot_home_compact_specialty.title: Compact 10x15 | crafting and enchanting
bot_home_compact_specialty.description: 10x15 specialty floor. All nine specialty stations and a crafting table; complete 15-bookshelf ring with a clear gap and entrance. Upstairs barrels omitted to keep circulation open. No furnaces.

bot_home_compact_beds_25.title: Compact 10x15 | approved 25-bed room
bot_home_compact_beds_25.description: Approved bedroom: 25 complete beds, 22 facing east and three facing south. Facing points from foot to head. West-wall south-facing pairs start at [1,1,8] and [1,1,10]; the third starts at [4,1,3]. Original block positions and circulation are preserved.

bot_home_compact_storage.title: Compact 10x15 | four balanced 39-barrel stations
bot_home_compact_storage.description: Architect storage layout: 156 barrels, four matching 39-barrel station allocations. Central supports [6,0,3], [6,0,7], [7,0,11], [3,0,11]. Rear allocations exchange the front pattern axes. Maximum assigned eye-to-centre reach is 3.043 blocks. Seven ceiling-hung lanterns retain the Architect's positions. Neighbouring barrels within 4.5 reach vary by station; assigned target lists preserve equal service capacity.

villager_home_compact_intake.description: DRAFT: exterior iron door, two carpeted chamber cells, then an interior normally closed fence gate. Stone buttons provide exterior and chamber door controls. villager_home_compact_jobs_10.name: villager_home_compact_jobs_10
villager_home_compact_jobs_10.title: Villager prototype | ten gated work stalls
villager_home_compact_jobs_10.description: DRAFT: ten gated one-standing-block stalls; carpet only on the ten resident standing cells. Fletching tables are profession placeholders; a second fence layer beside the stall stops climbing and the open cell above each table keeps the villager route inside the stall. Only expose one unclaimed job site during admission. Residents roam between the open stair and unassigned spaces; no admission/trading controller is installed.

villager_home_compact_breeding_25.name: villager_home_compact_breeding_25
villager_home_compact_breeding_25.title: Villager prototype | 25 beds and open circulation
villager_home_compact_breeding_25.description: DRAFT: original 25 bed pairs preserved. Open circulation between breeding room and job floor, with original stair edge rails retained. No containment cage or transfer gate. Ascending roof flight removed; cap remains closed. Breeding, sleep and worker bed release await live testing.

villager_home_compact_closed_roof.name: villager_home_compact_closed_roof
villager_home_compact_closed_roof.title: Villager prototype | closed roof cap
villager_home_compact_closed_roof.description: DRAFT: sealed stair opening with battlements. Golems may spawn on the roof and elsewhere in the base. Spawn prevention is limited to the airlock chamber and resident workstation spaces.

headframe.name: headframe
headframe.description: miningshaft covering with barrels and furnaces for building.
headframe.light_points_note: The door's two torches, outside and inside, each hung on the wall block over the door (lighting_integrity.designLamps, part 'door').
headframe.schema_note: this is the mining cover and first chest location. its purpose is to protect entry and exit of the main mining staircase and provide chests for pickup and dropoff. THE STATIONS ARE THREE STACKS ON EACH SIDE OF THE IDLE STAND (Architect 2026-10-22: "there should be 3 on each side of the headframe where the bot idles. on the bottom is the barrel laying down so you see it open and on the top is the furnace so there should be 6 furnace 5 barrel and one crafting table"): the room x -5..-3 has a line at z -1 and a line at z 1, the stand (-4,2,0) between them. Each stack is a barrel on its side with a furnace on it, both facing the stand (the z -1 line faces south, the z 1 line north); the middle of the z -1 line is the crafting table with anchor 0's furnace on it. Barrels, not chests, because a chest will not open under a furnace and a barrel does. THE OUTSIDE IS PLANKS (Architect 2026-10-22: "change the emergency shelter to only planks on the outside. forget the accents. its a shelter for the bots"); the only stone is the five furnaces. THE STACK NEAREST THE DOOR ON THE z 1 LINE IS THE COMPOSTER, WITH AIR OVER IT (Architect 2026-10-22: "make a composter as well. replace a row of furnace and barrel with composter closest to the door"): a full composter throws its bone meal out of its top, so nothing stands on it. THE TOP ROW IS BARRELS (Architect 2026-11-01: "the headframe was designed for 2 bots not 15. so bottom row is barrels, second row furnaces, top row barrel"): a barrel at y 4 over every furnace, the air over the composter kept. So the room holds 5 furnaces, 9 barrels, the crafting table and the composter.
headframe.anchor_order_note: ANCHOR ORDER IS A DEADLINE, NOT A LAYOUT. Anchors 0-2 are the SHELL and must stand before nightfall: floor, walls, roof, doors, plus the barrel, crafting table and furnace anchor 0 carries, because that is the minimum a fleet needs to share resources. A FURNACE AND A BARREL ARE ONE FITTING: smelting is batched for the whole fleet, so the bot that empties a furnace is usually not the bot that wanted the output, and output cannot go back into the furnace - the emptier must have somewhere to hand the surplus off. Anchor 0 is the only place in this fleet a furnace comes from; there is no pocket furnace and none is ever set down in a field. Everything that needs a surveyed MINE sits below the deadline: anchor 3 holds the rest of the stations (3 barrels, 4 furnaces, the composter). Anchors build in order and each is gated on holding ALL of its materials, so a voxel whose material comes from an unfinished chain stops the walls going up until that chain delivers. Do not move an ORE-dependent voxel into anchors 0-2.

underground_cell.name: underground_cell
underground_cell.description: 5 cubed with a 3x2x3 room and anchor for fractal cell mining. equal attaching on all sides. Transpose origin is in center
underground_cell.light_points_note: The cell's one wall torch: head height over a floor stand, on the solid east wall beside a door, transpose-origin-relative (lighting_integrity.mineLamps).

architect_staircase_landing.name: Architect_staircase_Landing
architect_staircase_landing.description: Quarter-turn landing between two staircase flights: enters like a flight descending east, leaves descending south
architect_staircase_landing.schema_note: Follows a flight, whose cells end at y=1 here; the next flight, its A on B and turned one quarter clockwise, starts at y=-2 and shares only the floor (2,-2,0). So the landing cannot disagree with either. The lane steps down at x=1 and x=2, then leaves south at (2,-2,1), where the flight above's wall is the ceiling. The air at z=1 and z=2 is the head room the next flight's first stands take from the piece before it, as a flight takes it from the flight above. A left turn is this piece mirrored in z (mining_blueprinter).

architect_staircase_final.name: Architect_staircase_Final
architect_staircase_final.description: 3-step diagonal descending staircase 3 wide: one walkway lane down the center, a solid wall on each side
architect_staircase_final.schema_note: GEOMETRY lives in anchors[].voxels; unassigned_voxels is empty. Voxels are transpose-origin-relative, NOT anchor-relative (collectAllVoxels pushes them raw, applying no offset) -- an anchor's position is its stand-spot, and the partition only records which stand paints each voxel; mining_executor re-assigns by reach at runtime regardless. TILING steps via attach points A(0,0,0)->B(3,-3,0) = +3,-3 per copy; repeat_offset is a DEAD FIELD read by no code -- do not trust its value. ONE LANE, THREE WIDE: the walkway is the center column z=0 and z=+-1 is solid wall wherever the walkway runs, so the body standing in the lane owns both walls and the ceiling above it. THE BOX IS FILLED SOLID ON PURPOSE (50 solid of 59 cells): a thin tube's walls are disjoint fragments -- measured 40 solid, largest face-connected group 22 -- and in rock the mountain seeds every fragment free, but in a cave nothing seeds a fragment whose every face is air. That is TessaBot's 5-loop judge-kill at 26|24|91: 3 ceiling voxels, all six neighbours air, unplaceable forever, and no ordering or retry can seed an empty set. A welded shell is ONE body, so a single attach face unzips the whole copy. Four cells stay UNDECLARED (x=2, y=-1..0, z=+-1): they are where a side-attached cell declares its door air; C and D sit in the wall plane z=+-1 directly under those doors, and mining_cell_graph:201 reads solid-vs-air as a contradiction and blackballs the cell -- the round-38 blackball, arriving from the other side. Undeclared, the cell owns them alone.
architect_staircase_final.light_points_note: A light point is the cell a wall torch stands in (position) and the block it hangs on (wall), transpose-origin-relative. Lit on every TORCH_NETWORK.stair_every-th copy from the top (lighting_integrity.mineLamps). (3,-1,0) is head height over the walkway's third stand; its wall (3,-1,1) is the solid south wall, clear of the side-attach door cells at x=2.

temp_construction_chest.name: temp_construction_chest
temp_construction_chest.description: when a building needs building, and the bots inventory does not have enough for the whole building then it places this blueprint reasonably close but not inside primary blueprint.

spawn_box.name: spawn_box
spawn_box.description: the 3 cubed interior of underground_cell with the walls taken off, plus the ground it rests on — one 3x3 layer of natural floor with 3 clear layers above it, so h=4. FOUND, NEVER BUILT: the arena searches for a place that already looks like this and drops a body in it; nothing pastes it. The floor layer is 'natural_block' to say what it IS (existing terrain, not something we lay) — it is NOT checked against the natural_block item group, because that group omits every ore and a cave floor is full of them; the runtime gate is site_geometry.isGround, which is deliberately looser. The arena reads its footprint from here, the way every other siter reads a blueprint, so retune the spawn box by editing these dimensions and nothing in the bench holds a copy of the number.

spawn_spot.name: spawn_spot
spawn_spot.description: spawn_box shrunk to a SINGLE column — one natural_block floor cell with 3 clear layers above it, so h=4 like its 3x3 sibling. FOUND, NEVER BUILT. It exists to be A/B tested against spawn_box (Architect 2026-07-31: "shrink the blueprint down to a single spot… i want to see if we can increase the matches while still making good line of sight"): the 3x3 footprint is the arena predicate's scarcest clause, so shrinking it is the cheapest way to raise the match rate. What it GIVES UP is the movement room the 3x3 was demanding — a body sited here is guaranteed to FIT and is not guaranteed to be able to MOVE, which is load-bearing because BRAWLER's counter is sprint knockback. It also re-admits the 'tiny 1 by 2 cave' the 3x3 clause was written to exclude. Read arena_sites' header before making this the default.

test_house.name: test_house
test_house.description: build bench fixture. a small house shell built from ONE stand, with stairs in every direction and both halves plus a chest facing away from the bot. nothing in the fleet builds it; only Auren_Workshop/tools/build_bench.js does.
test_house.schema_note: one house shell from a single stand (0,1,0). A voxel may carry a fifth element: the block state the finished cell must show, e.g. {"facing":"north","half":"top"}. The builder places such a voxel through place_authority -> facing_aim: the reported look is snapped onto the direction the rule needs for the click (stairs face the look; a chest faces opposite it) and any solid neighbour face in reach is clicked, seen or not (Architect 2026-09-16 Law 19 ruling), so no extra stand is needed for any facing. A0 floor level: bottom stairs facing east, west, north, south and a chest facing south, away from the stand. A1: wall tops carry upside-down stairs, north and south walls facing inward, west and east walls facing outward; the roof edge above them carries bottom stairs facing inward. Stair shape (corners) is decided by neighbours, not by the look, and is not asked for here.

laydown_yard.name: laydown_yard
laydown_yard.pledge_approved_note: EVERY BODY MAY PLACE AT ONCE, ONE CELL AT A TIME (Architect 2026-09-21: *'we will make blueprints explicitly labeled pledge approved. A pledge here isnt 9 blocks either its 1. If a bot can place one block then it does it. But it can claim as many as it can make. So the pledge of 1 is a minimum not a maximum... as long as the single block on the bottom is placed, the one above it can be placed.'*). The label is a CLAIM ABOUT THIS PLAN, checked at load by blueprint_registry.validatePledgeApproved: exactly one anchor, so there is no cube above a cube for a body to pillar into; and every placed voxel rests on the plan's own floor or on another placed voxel, so the per-cell support rule can always release the next block. Both are properties of the FILE, which is why they are refused on the developer's machine rather than discovered as a stalled crew.
laydown_yard.description: The builder crew's staging area for a downloaded building: 12 barrels, 13 furnaces, one crafting table and one composter, on open ground. Two parallel lines seven long, the lines 2 blocks apart: the south line is the crafting table at its west end and six barrels, with a furnace on each of the seven; the north line is the composter at its west end, with open air over it, and six barrels with a furnace on each (Architect 2026-10-20: the corner barrel and furnace became the composter again, because leaf litter and saplings are composted into bone meal for the wheat field).
laydown_yard.schema_note: HALVED FROM 24 CONTAINERS TO 12, AND THE REASON REPLACES THE ORIGINAL ONE (Architect 2026-09-20: *"cut the blueprint in half. We shouldnt need 24 chests and furnaces because were designing with throughput in mind. That material is going to be used as gathered. So it shouldnt fill up chests."*). The 2026-09-19 design sized this yard against a QUEUE — 24 separate containers so 20 bodies would not stand in one line — and that premise no longer holds: the bot band stopped banking at all (inventory_swapper.dropOffHaul), which took barrel traffic from 33.3 openings a minute to 3.1 and the container duty cycle from 90% to 3.6% in one run. Containers are no longer the constraint, so the yard is sized for what it actually holds rather than for a queue that stopped forming. WHY BARRELS AND NOT CHESTS is unchanged: a chest will not open with a solid block on top of it and a furnace is one, while a barrel opens whatever sits above it — so barrel-under-furnace is the stacking that keeps every container usable. THE FLOOR IS NATURAL GROUND (`natural_block`): the yard sits on the ground it is sited on. EACH FURNACE SITS ON A BARREL, except the one on the crafting table; furnace_executor's fitting is a furnace with a chest registered in the fleet, which the yard's barrels are. THE COMPOSTERS BECAME BARREL-AND-FURNACE PAIRS, THE TABLE CARRIES A FURNACE AND THE CORNER OPPOSITE IT A PAIR (Architect 2026-10-13: *"compost is pointless now that we have a waste pit. exchange the 2 compost bins for another layer of furnace and barrel... put another furnace ontop of the crafting table and another barrel and furnace opposit side so each size should have 7 furances, one side has 7 barrels, the other has 6 and a crafting table"*): 13 barrels and 14 furnaces in the footprint the 12 containers had. THE AISLE IS AIR TWO HIGH so a bot walks the middle and reaches both lines from it. THE CRAFTING TABLE IS PART OF THE BUILDING NOW, not wherever the first body to need one happened to stand: craft_handler.placeStation used to site a table at nearestPlaceableCell(bot), so the fleet's shared fixtures landed together only by luck (2026-09-19). It is placed in the gap column so it obstructs neither aisle lane. EVERY BARREL AND FURNACE FACES THE AISLE (Architect 2026-10-15: *"make the furnaces face inward and the barrels laydown so its uniform. all chests and furnaces should face inward on laydown yard"*): the south line (z -2) faces south and the north line (z 1) faces north, so each fixture opens toward the bot standing in the aisle, and a barrel lies on its side like the furnace on it. THE CORNER PAIR OPPOSITE THE TABLE IS THE COMPOSTER, WITH AIR OVER IT (Architect 2026-10-20: *"lets bring back compost bins then eh? now instead of a pit we exhcange the last barrel and furnace for compost bins"*): a full composter throws its bone meal out of its top as an item, so nothing stands on it; one bin serves the crew, because a visit feeds a whole banked batch at once and the bin is never the wait.
laydown_yard.anchor_order_note: ONE ANCHOR at (3,0,-1) — the floor voxel of the middle aisle — so a body STANDS at (3,1,-1), the aisle cell itself. THE +1 IS THE POINT AND IT COST A RUN: an anchor names the block a body's feet rest ON (locomotion.goToStand adds the +1, and every other blueprint in this file files its anchor on a solid voxel — planks, structural_fill, stand_ground). This anchor was authored at (3,1,-1), the aisle cell, which is authored `air` in this very voxel list — so goToStand demanded feet at (3,2,-1) with nothing under them, the navigator tried to pillar into the cell the body was already standing in, and gave up. On 2026-09-20 that was 37 of the run's 38 navigation failures and every one of the twenty bodies: the barrels were built and then unreachable, and the yard stalled at 31/53 because the builder could not reach its own stand either. Every block of the section — including the crafting table in the gap column at (0,1,-2) — is within 4.18 of the stand at (3,1,-1), inside the 4.5 reach; lowering the anchor a block IMPROVED the worst case, which was 4.77 and already over.
laydown_yard.lane_note: THE AISLE IS A ONE-WAY LANE, EAST TO WEST. A body bound for the anchor stand walks to ENTRY first (the east mouth, between the two lines' last barrels), then to the stand; a body leaving walks to EXIT first (the west mouth, in the gap column beside the crafting table), then on to wherever it is going. Both attach points follow the anchor convention: the floor block the feet rest ON. `interior` is the feet cells of the aisle between the two mouths; a route whose goal lies outside it may not enter it. `closed` is the two fixture lines, barrel level and furnace level, the whole length of each line: no route stands in a fixture's cell or on top of a barrel, built or not yet built. EXIT is the west mouth because the waste pit lies one block west of it, so a body leaving with trash is already at the rim.

lava_portal_mould.name: lava_portal_mould
lava_portal_mould.description: cobblestone mould a body casts a nether portal frame in, from lava buckets and one water bucket (action_fragments.js/lava_portal.js)
lava_portal_mould.design_intent: 48 cobblestone on level natural ground. The frame's low corner is blueprint (1,1,1), the frame stands in the plane z=1 and that plane is left empty. The casting stand is on the kerb at (3,2,3). The cap at y=6, z=2 takes each water pour; the lid at y=5, z=3 holds a settled source off the stand; the pillar at x=0, z=3 carries lid, roof and cap.

waste_pit.name: waste_pit
waste_pit.description: The builder crew's waste pit: a trench two blocks long and three deep in a 4x3 pad of natural ground, where a pocket's trash is thrown to despawn (custom_api/waste_pit). The ten cells round the trench are one level floor, open two high. A thrower stands on the pad cell at either end of the trench, in line with it, and throws along it at the block under the far end's stand. Sited by the foreman beside the laydown yard.
waste_pit.anchor_order_note: TWO ANCHORS, one at each end of the trench: (1,0,0) east and (-2,0,0) west. An anchor names the block the feet rest ON, so a body stands at (1,1,0) or (-2,1,0) and reaches its own half: the hole column beside it down to its floor, and the pad cells of its two columns. The transpose origin (0,0,0) is the east hole cell, at the pad's floor level; the west hole cell is (-1,0,0).

wheat_field.name: wheat_field
wheat_field.description: Every crew's wheat field: nine by nine on level ground, one water source at its centre and no fence. The rows run east-west and alternate grass, wheat, grass from the north edge to the south edge, so the five grass rows (z -4, -2, 0, 2, 4) hold the four wheat rows (z -3, -1, 1, 3) apart: a wheat cell has wheat only along its own row and grass on the other axis and on every diagonal, so no crop grows at the crowded rate (wheat_plot_scanner.growthPenalized). Every crop cell is within four blocks of the water, so all 36 are hydrated. The water stands in the middle grass row and is poured from a bucket; the grass rows are the walkways. Crop cells are the dirt voxels with a 'growing' voxel above (farmland_site); a grass cell is dirt with air above, walked on and never tilled. Sited by the foreman near the laydown yard and at least BLUEPRINT_SPACING from every other footprint; tended by the farming triad (assessors/farming, farm_manager, farm_executor). The water cell stands on a natural floor (y -1, natural_block: stone, gravel, dirt or any ground already there), so the hole is one deep; a deeper hole is filled to the floor before the water is poured, and ground already standing is never dug for it.
wheat_field.anchor_order_note: FIVE ANCHORS. An anchor names the block the feet rest ON. The first, at (1,0,0), stands beside the water cell in the middle grass row and owns only the water and the air over it: the bucket is poured from there, looking down into the hole, because from any other grass row the look passes over a crop cell first and would pour onto it. It is first so the water is in before the field is tilled. The other four stand on the grass rows at (-2,0,-2), (2,0,-2), (-2,0,2) and (2,0,2), and each owns the cells of its own quarter, all within 3.7 of its stand, inside the 4.5 reach. THE ORDER OF THE WORK: every block of the plan first (the floor, the rows, the walkways), then the water, then the tilling and planting (farm_executor).
wheat_field.attach_points_note: FOUR ATTACH POINTS. A copy attaches on a side by setting its opposite point on this one. North and south are cells of the edge grass rows, so two fields side by side SHARE that grass row (a copy eight south or north). East and west are the row ends: the rows run on from one field into the next, crop beside crop along the row, which grows at the uncrowded rate (a copy nine east or west). A copy attaches only on a side that takes it farther from the home.

sheep_pen.name: sheep_pen
sheep_pen.description: A crew's sheep pen (architect_config CREW_PROFILE farm_pen): an interior five wide (x -2..2) by sixteen long (z -8..7), 80 grass cells for 16 sheep at five each. The fence ring stands ON the grass layer (y 0 is dirt-family ground under the fence and the interior alike), so the grass runs unbroken under the fence and grows back into the pen. The gate is two wide (fence_gate at x 0 and x 1 in the south fence, z 8), because two followers wedge side by side in a one-wide doorway; herd_executor opens and shuts both (pen.gate, pen.side_gate). A herder holds the flock from outside the middle of a long side, so every interior cell is within the measured tempt reach. A one-block apron of natural ground and air runs down both long sides (x -4, x 4) and two rows south of the gate (z 9, 10): every build stand is out there, because a body has no way through a shut gate and would dig through the fence to leave. Sited beside the wheat field as near as the gap allows, on the surface (utils/surface_site): its floor is the middle height of the ground under it, cut and filled at most two layers, so it stays in the soil and the grass left at floor height spreads over the rest.
sheep_pen.anchor_order_note: NINE ANCHORS, every one outside the fence. Four stand on the west apron (x -4) at z -7, -2, 3 and 7 and own the west half (x -3..0); four on the east apron (x 4) at the same z own the east half (x 1..3); each owns the rows within two of its own z, so every cell is within BLOCK_REACH of the stand. The last stands two south of the gates at (0,0,10) and owns the south apron and both fence_gates: a fence gate faces the way its placer looks, so placing it while looking north gives a gate that swings on the pen's long axis and joins the south fence. It is last, so the pen shuts only once the rest stands. FOUR SECTIONS, one trip each (blueprint_registry.sectionOf): the west and east anchors of a stretch go together, A0+A4, A1+A5, A2+A6, then A3+A7 with the gate anchor A8 last, so one trip carries ten to fifteen fences and builds a quarter of the pen, each anchor still from its own stand outside the fence.

cow_pen.name: cow_pen
cow_pen.description: A crew's cow pen (architect_config CREW_PROFILE farm_pens, HERDING.pens.cow_pen), the sheep pen's geometry for cows: an interior five wide (x -2..2) by sixteen long (z -8..7), 80 grass cells for 16 cows at five each; a full pen keeps its breeding stock and the rest are culled for beef and leather (assessors/ranching). The fence ring stands ON the grass layer (y 0 is dirt-family ground under the fence and the interior alike), so the grass runs unbroken under the fence and grows back into the pen. The gate is two wide (fence_gate at x 0 and x 1 in the south fence, z 8), because two followers wedge side by side in a one-wide doorway; herd_executor opens and shuts both (pen.gate, pen.side_gate). A herder holds the flock from outside the middle of a long side, so every interior cell is within the measured tempt reach. A one-block apron of natural ground and air runs down both long sides (x -4, x 4) and two rows south of the gate (z 9, 10): every build stand is out there, because a body has no way through a shut gate and would dig through the fence to leave. Sited beside the wheat field as near as the gap allows, on the surface (utils/surface_site): its floor is the middle height of the ground under it, cut and filled at most two layers, so it stays in the soil and the grass left at floor height spreads over the rest.
cow_pen.anchor_order_note: NINE ANCHORS, every one outside the fence. Four stand on the west apron (x -4) at z -7, -2, 3 and 7 and own the west half (x -3..0); four on the east apron (x 4) at the same z own the east half (x 1..3); each owns the rows within two of its own z, so every cell is within BLOCK_REACH of the stand. The last stands two south of the gates at (0,0,10) and owns the south apron and both fence_gates: a fence gate faces the way its placer looks, so placing it while looking north gives a gate that swings on the pen's long axis and joins the south fence. It is last, so the pen shuts only once the rest stands. FOUR SECTIONS, one trip each (blueprint_registry.sectionOf): the west and east anchors of a stretch go together, A0+A4, A1+A5, A2+A6, then A3+A7 with the gate anchor A8 last, so one trip carries ten to fifteen fences and builds a quarter of the pen, each anchor still from its own stand outside the fence.

water_pool.name: water_pool
water_pool.description: Every crew's water pool: four by four on level ground, a square of four water cells (x 0..1, z 0..1) in a rim of dirt. Water with source water on two sides over solid ground is a source itself, so every cell of the square refills the moment a bucket takes it: the crew's one endless water (land_prep's well), every field's pour filled here. Sited beside the wheat field after the pens, before any other field, and laid first of the farm's sites (it opens FARM_FIELD.keys), so the fields' water comes from it. Built by the farming triad; it grows no crop. The square stands on a natural floor (y -1, natural_block: stone, gravel, dirt or any ground already there), so the pool is one deep; a deeper one is filled to the floor before the water is poured, and ground already standing is never dug for it.
water_pool.anchor_order_note: TWO ANCHORS. An anchor names the block the feet rest ON. The first, at (-1,0,0) on the west rim, owns the two water cells on one diagonal, (0,0,0) then (1,0,1): two pours, and the other two cells, each between two sources, become sources themselves. It is first so the water is in before the second anchor reads its cells. The second, at (2,0,1) on the east rim, owns the other diagonal (1,0,0) and (0,0,1), which it finds standing as sources (farm_executor takes a water cell already a source as placed), and the east and south rim. THE ORDER OF THE WORK: every block of the plan first (the floor, the rows, the walkways), then the water, then the tilling and planting (farm_executor).

cane_field.name: cane_field
cane_field.description: Every crew's sugar cane field: eight by five on level ground. One water channel six long (x -3..2, z 0), every cell a source poured from a bucket filled at the crew's water pool, so the water stands still and carries no cut piece off, with a row of sugar cane on each side of it (z -1 and z 1), twelve plants, each planted on the dirt beside the water and never tilled. A walkway of dirt runs round the field (z -2, z 2, and the ends x -4 and x 3), the stands for every plant. Crop cells are the dirt voxels with a 'growing' voxel above (farmland_site); the cell above a plant is left out of the plan, because the cane grows into it. The crop is sugar_cane (farmland_site CROPS): planted from the cane item, ripe once two tall, cut from the second block up so the bottom one regrows. Sited in the farm ring, outside the ring of the building, the yard, the pens and the pool; its copies (cane_field_2 and on, as many as calculators/cane_critical_mass asks for) attach to it and to each other by their attach points, touching, and grow away from the home (lock_all_buildspots siteFieldCluster); tended by the farming triad (assessors/farming, farm_manager, farm_executor) in one visit with the wheat field. Every channel cell stands on a natural floor (y -1, natural_block: stone, gravel, dirt or any ground already there), so the channel is one deep; a deeper one is filled to the floor before the water is poured, and ground already standing is never dug for it.
cane_field.anchor_order_note: FIVE ANCHORS. An anchor names the block the feet rest ON. The first, at (-4,0,0), stands on the walkway at the channel's west end and owns the channel's first two water cells and the air over them: the bucket is poured from there, looking down the channel into its first cell, because from a side walkway the look passes over a plant's dirt first and would pour onto it. Every channel cell is a source (farm_executor pours each cell holding only water that ran into it): the first two pours run water east along the channel, and once the cell between two sources is one the rest refill from it. It is first so the water is in before any cane is planted; the four other channel cells belong to the side anchors in reach of them. The other four stand on the side walkways at (-2,0,-2), (2,0,-2), (-2,0,2) and (2,0,2), and each owns the cells of its own quarter within the 4.5 reach. THE ORDER OF THE WORK: every block of the plan first (the floor, the rows, the walkways), then the water, then the tilling and planting (farm_executor).
cane_field.attach_points_note: FOUR ATTACH POINTS, one on each side, each a cell of that side's walkway. A copy attaches on a side by setting its opposite point on this one (its N on this S, its W on this E), so two touching strips SHARE the walkway between them: a strip beside it four south (or north), a strip after it seven east (or west). The rows read cane, water, cane, walkway, cane, water, cane, and every plant stays beside a walkway. A copy attaches only on a side that takes it farther from the home.
